description: AletheiaDB Performance Targets - Single source of truth for performance goals

targets.rationale: Zero temporal overhead for non-temporal queries
Direct anchor lookup with minimal overhead
Delta application for mid-range historical queries
Acceptable for compliance and audit queries

Absolute ceiling on the MCP protocol + parse + dispatch + handler latency of a tool call through the shipped aletheia-mcp stdio server, measured under an Async durability profile (Issue #3361). This is an MCP-layer metric, NOT durable-write latency: the default durable GroupCommit{max_delay_ms:10} adds ~10ms of batch-wait to a solo write, which is a WAL/durability cost paid equally by any caller (it cancels out of the overhead sub-metric) and is out of scope for this gate. Gated per-scenario; the absolute ceiling catches gross blowups. Hard-failed (exit 3) in the nightly lane.

targets.metric: MCP round-trip p50 vs committed reference baseline (same gated set)
targets.rationale: Relative regression gate: a gated scenario whose current median (p50) exceeds 2x its committed baseline p50 fails (Issue #3361). Gates on the median (stable +-3-9% run-to-run) rather than p99 (tail drifts >10% and would false-fail). Needed because the honest gated p99 sits ~26x under the 5ms absolute ceiling, so a clean 2x regression would otherwise stay green. Baseline at benchmarks/baselines/mcp_round_trip_baseline.json; hard-failed (exit 4) in the nightly lane.

targets.metric: MCP transport overhead (round-trip minus in-process direct call)
targets.rationale: JSON-RPC serialization + stdio + process-boundary cost above the direct API floor for single-entity reads (Issue #3361). Independently checkable per scenario via the overhead sub-metric. Note: overhead percentiles subtract independently-sorted round-trip and direct series (unpaired), so p95/p99 overhead is an informational decomposition, noisy on the tail; the p50 is the reliable central estimate. Informational, never gated.

Issue #3383: on the CPU-bound arm (Async 1ms-flush, interleaved multi-pass, solo DB per config, so per-write trust CPU cost bottlenecks throughput) write throughput with #3224 provenance + #3218 uniqueness constraint enabled must stay >=80% of the same-run no-trust baseline (measured back-to-back, hardware-variance-immune). Composed folds the two per-write-CPU trust features; the #3351 chain is measured separately (see chain_active note)
Issue #3383: on the CPU-bound arm, attaching a #3224 provenance bundle to every write must keep throughput >=85% of the same-run baseline (WAL serializes extra source/confidence/note bytes)
Issue #3383: on the CPU-bound arm, an active #3218 uniqueness constraint must keep write throughput >=85% of the same-run baseline (per-write reservation-index check on the commit path)

Issue #3383: the #3351 tamper-evident hash chain is an async SHA-256 sealer sidecar. At the CPU-bound arm's ~100K+ writes/sec the sealer, not the writer's per-write enqueue CPU, is the throughput ceiling on a slow shared core, so the CPU-arm ratio measures sealer throughput (observed ~0.63-0.84) not per-write cost -- it is reported but NOT hard-gated here. The chain's >=0.90 overhead metric is owned and gated by the dedicated provenance_chain bench (Issue #3351) in its native GroupCommit regime

Issue #3383: on the CPU-bound arm, attaching a #3371 fact-to-fact derivation-lineage list (fixed small derived_from set) to every write must keep throughput >=80% of the same-run baseline (per-write in-memory lineage-index insert + source validation costs ~12%; bound set well below observed ~0.86-0.91 for shared-runner headroom)
Issue #3383 (AC4): carrying provenance must not slow the current-state single-hop read hot path
Issue #3383 (AC4): reconstructing a provenance-carrying historical version stays within the temporal-query budget
Issue #3383 (AC5): crash recovery of a provenance + uniqueness-constraint dataset at the 10K-node/50K-edge reference scale completes within the medium-dataset recovery budget
